title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-03
content:
2026-03-03 (Tue) - quick brain dump / daily TODOs

Morning goals:
- triage high-pri perf regressions from last deploy (release v2.14.1)
- run microbench for attention kernel with 8k context on A100s
- validate kv-cache eviction fix in staging

Standups / meetings:
- 10:00 sync w/ SRE on autoscaler throttling (Andrew)
- 11:30 PR review w/ Lina (kernel patch, WIP)
- 15:00 postmortem follow-up (low-latency alerts)

Bug triage (quick notes):
- BUG-1120: spike in tail latency for short requests after last rollback
  - reproduced locally when batch size bursts > 64 and heavy kv-cache churn
  - hypothesis: eviction path holding a global lock -> stalls scheduling thread
  - immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch to 48 on canary pool (deployed to canary at 08:45)
  - long-term: per-shard eviction + lock-free ring (see kernel TODOs)

- BUG-1137: tokenizer mismatch for some multilingual prompts (reported by QA)
  - repro: emoji + zh text -> token IDs differ between v2.14.0 and v2.14.1
  - root cause: sentencepiece update in vendored tokenizer; revert vendor until compatibility test added

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- microbench: attention kernel (matmul-fused)
  - machine: a100-40gb, p3dn-like memory profile
  - config: seq-len = [512, 2048, 8192], batch = [1,8,32], kv-cache enabled
  - metric: tokens/sec, 95th latency
  - capture: nvprof + serving-runtime traces (trace-id: perf-20260303-01)
  - note: try disabling prefetch to see impact on memory thrash

- batching experiment: adaptive max_batch based on queue depth
  - previous setup (prod): static max_batch = 64
  - proposal: max_batch = min(64, 8 + floor(queue_depth / 16)) -> should avoid big bursts
  - A/B allocate 10% of traffic to new policy (need SRE approval)

Kernel notes / design ideas:
- KV-cache eviction: current single global LRU list causes lock contention under churn
  - idea: per-device shards with local LRUs + best-effort background compaction thread
  - alternative: multi-producer single-consumer queue per shard for evict events
  - ensure TTL-based fast-path for known short-lived prefixes (from telemetry)

- Attention kernel: fused matmul + rotary ops currently wins for seq <= 2048
  - at 8k sequence, memory layout penalizes tensor-core utilization -> try split attention (chunked rotary)
  - consider half-precision accumulation tweaks (FP16 accumulate to TF32 where safe)

Quick results / numbers (from yesterday):
- baseline (v2.14.0) 1k-seq, batch=8: 12k tok/s, p95 = 120ms
- v2.14.1 (after small kernel change): 1k-seq, batch=8: 9.2k tok/s, p95 = 220ms -> unacceptable
- canary reverted to v2.14.0 reduced p95 to ~130ms

Action items (me):
- [ ] finish lock-free eviction prototype (branch: kv-evict-shards) -> target PR by EOD Fri
- [ ] run attention microbench for 8k sequences + post raw traces to perf dashboard
- [ ] add compatibility test for sentencepiece vendor change (CI)
- [ ] follow up with SRE on autoscaler knobs; propose safe defaults for canary pools

Notes to self:
- keep short-latency SLO doc linked in PRs (remind reviewers to check p95 impact)
- add a small README in kernel/ explaining tradeoffs of fused vs chunked attention
- ask Lina to pair on noisy-lock repro tomorrow morning

Random TODOs (small):
- tidy up perf-20260228 logs on GCS (delete older than 90d)
- update rollout checklist with "verify tokenizer vendor" step

End.
